speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me exactly which arm is affected and whether the pain radiates from your neck down into specific fingers? Additionally, did this issue start suddenly after an injury or come on gradually over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. I need to clarify if the weakness and paresthesias are symmetric in both hands, and do you experience any difficulty with balance, walking, or bowel and bladder control? Also, does the pain worsen with specific neck movements, such as looking up or turning your head?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The presence of fasciculations, absent reflexes, and bilateral hand weakness with paresthesias raises concern for motor neuron disease or severe cervical myelopathy. I will request an MRI of the cervical spine to evaluate for structural compression, and an EMG/Nerve Conduction Study to assess for motor neuron involvement.
